description: Family 4: The Clarkes. Two working parents — one earning above threshold, the other with adjusted net income over £100k. Demonstrates the sharp cliff edge where exceeding £100k blocks both the 30-hour working parent entitlement and Tax-Free Childcare, leaving only the 15-hour universal entitlement for the 3-year-old.

costEstimate.description: Worked example for the Clarke family. One parent earns above the minimum threshold; the other has adjusted net income over £100,000. This triggers a sharp cliff edge: the family is blocked from the 30-hour working parent entitlement and Tax-Free Childcare. The only government support remaining is the 15-hour universal entitlement for 3- and 4-year-olds.

olivia.narrative: Olivia attends Henleaze Day Nursery (provider_11) for 5 morning sessions per week. The nursery operates 51 weeks per year. At age 3, she qualifies for the 15-hour universal entitlement. However, because one parent has income over £100,000, the family is blocked from the additional 15 working-parent hours. The provider's effective hourly rate (£7.20/hr) exceeds the Bristol government funding rate (£5.46/hr), creating a £1.74/hr shortfall.

step1_childcareFees.note: Using provider_11 age 3-4 rate: £36.00 per morning session

step3_fundedHoursReduction.unfundedTermTimeHours: 25 hrs/week - 15 funded = 10 unfunded hrs/week × 38 weeks = 380 hrs × £7.20 = £2,736.00

blockedEntitlements.workingParent30Hours: BLOCKED — one parent has adjusted net income over £100,000.

jack.narrative: Jack is school-age. His term-time care consists of a free breakfast club and after-school club at Westbury-on-Trym CofE Primary School (provider_12). Holiday cover is provided by Bristol North West Holiday Club (provider_19). No funded hours apply. Because the family is blocked from Tax-Free Childcare by the £100k threshold, all costs are entirely self-funded.

jackTotal.note: Jack is school-age with no funded hours. TFC blocked by £100k threshold. Free breakfast club saves £1,140 compared to a paid club at £6/session.

totalCostOfChildcare.description: The total annual cost of all childcare for this family, before any government support is applied.

fundedHours.note: Government pays 15 hrs × £5.46 × 38 wks = £3,112.20 to provider. Parent pays the £1.74/hr shortfall directly.

familyTotal.summaryNote: This family's childcare costs £12,910 per year. The government contributes just £3,112 (24%) — solely through the 15-hour universal entitlement for Olivia. Because one parent earns over £100,000, the family is locked out of the 30-hour entitlement and Tax-Free Childcare. The family pays £9,798 out of pocket.

cliffEdgeAnalysis.description: The £100,000 adjusted net income threshold creates one of the sharpest cliff edges in the childcare support system.
cliffEdgeAnalysis.additionalFundedHours: 15 hrs × 38 weeks = 570 additional hours for Olivia. Saving: £3,112.20.
cliffEdgeAnalysis.taxFreeChildcareGain: Up to £4,000 per year (£2,000 per child × 2 children)
cliffEdgeAnalysis.totalLostSupport: Up to £7,112.20 per year in combined lost benefits
cliffEdgeAnalysis.effectiveMarginalRate: Earning £1 over the £100,000 threshold costs this family up to £7,112 in lost childcare support.
